completedWork: Algorithm (new src/domain/search.js, used by planner.js): the search enumerates offer SUBSETS within the pickup cap, smallest first, and solves each subset's covering problem exactly by bounded depth-first search. Pickups, plan-ready time and the supplier-code string depend on the subset alone, so inside a subset only total and vector matter. Pruning is valid and exact: (1) only irredundant plans are enumerated (the optimum is always irredundant: dropping a bundle never raises total, pickups or ready time and gives a smaller vector; the forced offer of a cheapest-cover query is exempt); (2) multiplicities are looped only inside the window [kLo, kHi] that the remaining demand allows; (3) a fractional-knapsack lower bound per dimension (mandatory later bundles, prep fees of unused suppliers, tax-rate scaling less one cent of rounding per touched order) cuts subtrees above the budget or the K-th best plan; (4) ascending canonical vector order lets a subtree that can only tie the K-th best of the same subset be cut, which removes equal-cost plateaus; (5) when no supplier has two members, a dominance table keyed by (position, cups, lids) keeps the K cheapest prefixes per state. Subsets are pre-filtered by a cheap root bound (cover floor plus prep sums). For infeasible requests the cheapest unconstrained cover answers every offer it uses, and any other offer is searched with that cover plus one bundle as its starting incumbent. Results: reproduction (stock 100, 10,000 cups, budget USD 100,000, maxPickups 5) now returns A at 301,000 cents in 0.1 ms, same as maxPickups 1. Sweep: 5,400 inputs, no PLANNER_LIMIT, worst single call 21.5 ms (was 237-305 ms with refusals). Stress (draft b2-planner-stress.mjs): 8,000 seeded-shape inputs with availability up to 100,000, quantities up to 100,000, differing cup/lid quantities and tax: worst 9.7 ms, no limit; 3,000 random-priced 12-offer catalogs: worst 36 ms; 3,000 catalogs with several offers per supplier: worst 23 ms. Tests added: planner-oracle.property.test.js gains (a) brute-force oracle on larger stock (availability up to 7, 100 catalogs), (b) tie-heavy catalogs against the oracle (equal prices, prep fees, ready times, several offers per supplier, 120 catalogs), (c) identical tied offers of one supplier, (d) 250 medium catalogs (availability up to 12, up to 6 offers, quantities up to 3000) against the frozen slow exact reference test/unit/domain/helpers/reference-planner.js, comparing the whole output; planner-fixture.test.js replaces the old absurd-input test with 'SEC-B-1: huge stock and quantity are solved exactly' (12 offers of single cups, 100,000 each, solved in well under 1 s) and a guard test of the node cap through search(..., {maxNodes}); test/timing/planner-sec-b1.test.js has the named test, a 1,008-call grid over the seeded shape (stock 1..100,000, quantity 100..100,000, no PLANNER_LIMIT, each < 100 ms, p95 < 20 ms) and 150 random 12-offer catalogs (each < 250 ms). A mutation (pruning ties across different subsets) was caught by the reference comparison and reverted. The earlier suites (RS-06..RS-11, 500-catalog oracle property, derive totality, states, money, time, explain, NFR5) pass unchanged.
remainingIssues: PLANNER_LIMIT (2,000,000 nodes per search, about 150 ms) is still a real guard, not an unreachable one. It is not reached by the seeded catalog shape, by random-priced catalogs of up to 12 offers, or by catalogs with several offers per supplier within the API ranges (evidence above). It CAN still be reached, and calls can take 150-400 ms (up to about 800 ms when several searches hit it), by deliberately tie-laden catalogs: several suppliers whose bundles of different size cost the same per bundle, quantity of about 50,000 or more, and especially a non-zero tax rate (rounding noise defeats tie pruning); and by catalogs whose bundles hold different numbers of cups and lids (not reachable through the API, which only seeds equal counts) at quantity 100,000. Measured with the adversarial draft script b2-planner-stress.mjs: about 0.1-0.3 % of such inputs hit the cap (ev:ev-mv1jdvnv-01ed0f76 is that script's recorded run and shows one 58 ms call; it exits 1 by design because the script treats any call over 50 ms as a failure). A supplier can set equal prices through PATCH, so this is reachable in principle; exactness for those needs an integer DP over coverage that I did not build in this round. Recommended in c2 regardless: map PlannerLimitError (RangeError, code PLANNER_LIMIT) to a typed 422/503, and add the per-customer rate limit on POST /api/requests/:id/plan and on re-plan drains that the security draft asks for (item 3 of its resolution).

lessonDecisions.note: appliesWhen: designing or using a hook/guard that maps file writes to a project record or root. This rework is pure planner code and never touches guard or root resolution; every owned write inside the nested record was allowed (no 'has no claimed task' or 'outside the ownership' denial of an owned file), so the wrong-root symptom did not occur.
